headline: Approved July 28 minutes; tabled officer election and FY27 workplan; continued review of building typology recommendations.

Tabled the reorganization and election of officers to the next meeting.
Tabled the FY27 workplan to the next meeting.
Tabled City, Council, and Inclusion & Belonging Commission updates to the next meeting.

decision_titles: City, Council, and Inclusion & Belonging Commission updates
plain_text:
8/25/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
The meeting was called to order at 6:00 PM by Jack Commo, Vice-Chair.
Commissioners present: Jack Commo Vice-Chair, Jaqueline Thomas, Jarron Khan.
City Staff present: Jazmine Hurley Housing Initiative Director, Ravi Venkataraman
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
No public comment was received.
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
A motion to approve the July 28, 2026 meeting minutes was made by Jack and seconded by 
Jaqueline. Motion passed unanimously. Meeting began at 6:01pm.
Discussion: Building Typologies Report Overview
Ravi presented the Residential Building Typology Analysis, a planning project completed with 
support from the Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission (CCRPC). The project 
used approximately $60,000–$70,000 in federal transportation planning funds focused on transit-
oriented development.
The project had two primary objectives: developing residential design standards that reflect the 
City's desired development patterns and evaluating whether the City's existing Priority Housing 
regulations and lot coverage incentives effectively support the development of affordable, family-
sized housing.
l Consultants developed models showing how different housing types could fit on typical 
Winooski residential lots while accounting for lot coverage, setbacks, parking, building 
access, and internal unit layouts. 
l The models focused particularly on family-sized housing and generally assumed three-
bedroom units of at least 1,200 square feet. 
l Most models demonstrated that family-sized housing could be accommodated within 
the City's existing 50% lot coverage requirement. One model on a larger/deeper lot 
required exceeding the 50% threshold. 
l Consultants noted the prevalence of front porches in Winooski's existing residential 
neighborhoods and recommended excluding front porches from lot coverage calculations 
as an incentive to maintain this characteristic in new development. 
l Additional recommendations included increasing the standard lot coverage allowance 
from 50% to 55%, revising how building height is measured to better preserve the City's 
existing two- to two-and-a-half-story development pattern, and considering allowing up to 
eight units within a single building in certain residential areas. 
l Staff discussed infrastructure considerations associated with placing multiple buildings 
on a single lot. Public Works has expressed interest in configurations that reduce the 
number and complexity of separate water and wastewater connections.
The Planning Commission is continuing to review the recommendations, particularly potential 
changes related to lot coverage, building height, and the number of units permitted within a 
building.
Commissioners discussed utility connections, setbacks, front porches, preservation of usable 
rear-yard space, and the proposed changes to building-height measurements. Staff clarified that 
the models generally operate within the City's existing setback requirements.
Discussion/Approval: Reorganization and Election of Officers
This item was tabled to the next meeting.
Discussion: FY27 Workplan
This item was tabled to the next meeting.
Discussion: FY26 LL Survey Data Results
Jazmine presented results from the City's FY2025 landlord survey, which is distributed annually 
with the Public Building Registry mailing. The voluntary survey collects information on 
Winooski's rental housing stock, including unit sizes, rents, housing assistance, rental 
availability, rent increases, and challenges reported by property owners.
l The survey represented 185 properties owned by 158 landlords, approximately 60% of 
the City's public building rental stock. 
l Average reported monthly rents for all units were approximately $1,489 for studios, 
$1,744 for one-bedroom units, $2,000 for two-bedroom units, $2,100 for three-bedroom 
units, and $2,900 for units with four or more bedrooms. These averages include both 
market-rate and subsidized/affordable units. 
l Staff noted that reported rents may appear lower than rents currently advertised 
because the survey represents the City's entire rental stock, including long-term tenants 
in lower-cost units that rarely become available on the open market. 
l Approximately one in five respondents were owner-occupant landlords. 
l Of landlords responding to a question about applications received for unit openings, 
approximately 30% reported either no new lease or filling a unit through word of mouth. 
Most available units received approximately two to five applications. 
l Staff noted indications that the rental market has become somewhat less constrained 
compared with the period immediately following the COVID-19 pandemic. 
l Of 149 landlords responding to a question about rent increases, approximately 56% 
reported raising rents. Most increases were between $50 and $100. 
l Taxes were the most frequently cited reason for rent increases. Other reported 
pressures included general inflation, property maintenance and improvements, insurance, 
utilities, Code requirements, and other operating costs.
City, Council, and Inclusion & Belonging Commission Updates 
This item was tabled to the next meeting.
Other Business
None.
Adjourn
Motion to end the meeting was made by Jack and seconded by Jaqueline. Motion passed 
unanimously. Meeting ended at 7:03pm.
